author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is preparing a large study of people who were children near the World Trade Center when the towers fell, addressing a major gap in long-term September 11 health research.

Reuters reported that roughly 25,000 children lived or attended school near lower Manhattan in 2001, with thousands more in surrounding neighborhoods. Many encountered dust containing pulverized concrete, glass fibers, asbestos and other pollutants, yet few entered the government-funded studies that largely followed first responders and other adults.

The CDC plans to seek research applications for a World Trade Center Youth Research Coordinating Center and a long-term cohort. Eligible participants would have been 21 or younger, or in utero, and living below 14th Street in Manhattan or anywhere in Brooklyn on and after the attacks. Researchers also plan a similarly aged comparison group without the same exposure.

Key details, including the target number of participants, proposal date and available funding, have not been finalized publicly. Scientists hope the project can clarify possible links to cancers, cardiovascular disease and reproductive outcomes as the exposed population reaches its 30s and early 40s.
dek: The project will seek to identify and track people who were young, infants or in utero near lower Manhattan and Brooklyn after the attacks.
headline: CDC plans major health study of children exposed to 9/11
